connections.why: Global urban processes mirror change in UK places
Economic change drives differences in development
Both landscapes are shaped by water processes and management
Rising seas intensify coastal flooding and erosion
Climate change threatens fragile ecosystems and biodiversity
Understanding ecosystems underpins their sustainable management
Development must balance growth with environmental limits
Fieldwork relies on mapping sample sites accurately
Field data is presented and tested with graphs and statistics
Collected data is then analysed to reach conclusions
Analysing an issue leads to a justified decision
Development conflicts are common problem-solving contexts
Coastal management decisions are classic issue scenarios
Maps reveal coastal landforms and management schemes
Population and economic data are interpreted statistically
